prose:
People edit the prose after the first review. When the prose is extracted again, an intent with the same
statement keeps its verdict and its approvals. If a reviewer amended an intent and the AI proposes its original
reading again for the same words, the amendment is applied again. Everything else comes back as proposed, so only
what the edit changed needs a new look. A decision asked again with the same question keeps its answer.

decisions.question: When an amendment is applied again, do the approvals of the amended wording come back too?

options.label: Yes, keep them
options.consequence: The reviewed wording is unchanged, so nobody has to approve it again.

options.label: No, approve again
options.consequence: Every edit near an amended intent sends it back to the reviewers.

decisions.question: Does "the same statement" (or question) ignore letter case and spacing?

options.label: Ignore case and spacing
options.consequence: Re-wrapping a line or changing capitalization does not reopen the review.

options.label: Exact text only
options.consequence: Any cosmetic change in the AI's wording reopens the review of that intent.

notPromised: That decisions raised by the consistency check, and the intents created from their answers, survive a new extraction.
That an intent keeps its id (I1, I2...) when intents are added or removed above it.
